strengths: Clear and well-motivated problem: identifies concrete limitations in prior LLM-based AHD methods and proposes principled solutions through Hindsight and Foresight mechanisms
Significant practical improvements: 3-5× reduction in LLM query count and 4-10× faster training across all evaluated domains, demonstrating tangible efficiency gains

Comprehensive experimental evaluation: multiple problem domains (TSP, BPP, FSSP, BO), strong baselines, detailed ablations (Table 5) showing both components contribute, convergence analysis, and out-of-distribution testing (TSPLib)
Excellent reproducibility: complete algorithms, full prompt templates in appendices, explicit hyperparameter specifications, and sufficient implementation details for reproduction
Rigorous technical execution: well-designed utility-based credit assignment with EMA smoothing, principled regime selection logic, and adaptive pruning for insight pool maintenance
Consistent improvements across domains: outperforms EoH, ReEvo, HSEvo, and MCTS-AHD on all four problem types tested
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: Insight Pool is essentially Cultural Algorithms' Belief Space (acknowledged); Foundation Prompts adapted from EoH; main contribution is integration of existing ideas rather than new techniques

Static Evolutionary Navigator: uses fixed, handcrafted thresholds (Tstag, Tprog, Δcrit) calibrated per-problem, lacking true adaptivity; no learning mechanism to adjust thresholds online—contradicts 'adaptive control' framing and acknowledged as major limitation by authors

Intra-task knowledge learning: Insight Pool only learns within single problems; cross-domain transfer not systematically evaluated; severely limits practical generalizability of 'self-evolving' knowledge base

Arbitrary design choices insufficiently justified: credit assignment piecewise constants (0.8, 0.2, 0.2, 0.6, -0.3, 0.5) appear unmotivated; Jaccard threshold (0.7), pool capacity (30), and grace period (3) lack principled justification; no sensitivity analysis on 11+ hyperparameters

Lack of theoretical grounding: no formal analysis of why Foresight+Hindsight outperforms alternatives, no convergence guarantees, and claim about non-linear evolutionary contribution (Eq. 3) is unsupported

Experimental fairness concerns: different baselines use different seed functions; limited out-of-distribution evaluation; BO results (Table 9) show inconsistent improvements; missing statistical significance tests (no confidence intervals or error bars); very small population sizes (4 individuals, 8 generations) may not reflect scalability
Specification gaps: recency bonus Br in Eq. 1 not fully defined; Algorithm 1 line 17 condition for wisdom extraction is vague; Eq. 7 regime selection precedence unclear when multiple conditions hold
Marginal improvements in some domains: BPP gains only 0.66% vs 0.79% for HSEvo; FSSP improvements modest in absolute terms; raises questions about statistical significance
Figure 1 dense and difficult to parse; presentation could be more concise (28 pages is lengthy); core contributions could be distilled more clearly

strengths: Well-motivated research direction addressing knowledge accumulation and adaptive control in LLM-based AHD
Comprehensive empirical evaluation across multiple problem types (TSP, BPP, FSSP, BO) with diverse baselines and out-of-distribution testing
Clear technical presentation with detailed framework architecture, mathematical formulations, and extensive appendices
Ablation studies demonstrating contributions of individual components
Demonstrated improvements in convergence speed and LLM query efficiency
weaknesses: Unfair experimental comparisons: method leverages seed insights from literature (Appendix G.2) not provided to baselines, giving significant initialization advantage
Limited novelty: primarily combines existing techniques (Cultural Algorithms' Belief Space, Adaptive Operator Selection, EoH foundation) without sufficient innovation for a top-tier venue

Arbitrary design choices lacking justification: credit assignment coefficients (Eq. 3), fixed thresholds for Navigator (Eq. 7), utility function weights—no ablation studies or sensitivity analysis provided
Static control policy cannot learn or adapt thresholds (Tstag=3, Tprog=2, Δcrit=0.3); unclear if these were tuned on test problems (potential test-set contamination)
Lack of statistical rigor: no significance tests, confidence intervals only in one figure, ablation studies show single runs with no error bars, n=5 insufficient for reliable conclusions
Intra-task knowledge severely limits applicability: Insight Pool cannot transfer across different problem types; no cross-domain evaluation
Reproducibility concerns: many hyperparameters (13+ listed) without justification; code unavailable (proprietary API); no sensitivity analysis
Confounding variables in efficiency comparison: different population sizes (4 vs. 10) make training time and convergence comparisons problematic
Highly variable generalization: Table 6 shows performance ranging from 3.81% to 40.30% gap with no analysis of failure cases
Incomplete technical specifications: Algorithm 1 line 17 condition undefined, Algorithm 3 normalization unclear, Eq. 7 AND/OR precedence unspecified

strengths: Well-motivated framework combining hindsight (knowledge accumulation via Insight Pool) and foresight (adaptive control via Evolutionary Navigator) that directly addresses documented limitations in existing LLM-based AHD methods

Comprehensive experimental evaluation across four diverse optimization domains (TSP, Online BPP, FSSP, BO) with systematic comparisons against handcrafted heuristics, neural methods, and LLM-based baselines
Strong practical results: consistent improvements over baselines, 5-10× reduction in LLM requests, faster convergence with smaller populations, and significant wall-clock speedups
Rigorous technical presentation with detailed mathematical formulations (Eqs. 1-7), credit assignment mechanisms, and principled regime selection logic
Comprehensive appendices enabling reproducibility: prompt templates, algorithm pseudocode, hyperparameters, and extensive additional results (TSPLib, Weibull instances)
Effective ablation studies (Table 5) demonstrating meaningful contributions of both Hindsight and Foresight components
Clear visual presentation (Figures 1-4) and generally well-structured methodology
weaknesses: Moderate conceptual novelty: Insight Pool explicitly adapts Cultural Algorithms' 'Belief Space' (existing idea), and Evolutionary Navigator uses hand-crafted rule-based control similar to classical EC parameter control; work primarily combines existing mechanisms rather than introducing fundamentally new concepts

Critical limitation on knowledge generalization: insights are entirely task-specific with no cross-domain transfer evaluation; authors acknowledge in Appendix E.1 that 'generalizability across different problem domains remains unevaluated'—contradicts claims about learning from experience

Static and problem-dependent control logic: Navigator thresholds (Tstag=3, Tprog=2, Δcrit=0.3) are hand-tuned for evaluated problems; authors acknowledge these 'may not be universally optimal' with no systematic guidance for new problems; no learned meta-controller despite it being natural here

Insufficient analysis of Insight Pool quality: no evaluation of insight extraction quality, diversity, or reliability; Jaccard similarity threshold (0.7) appears arbitrary without justification; no evidence that higher-utility insights meaningfully improve performance

Experimental methodology concerns: inconsistent population sizes across comparisons (HiFo-Prompt: 4 vs EoH: 10-20), no statistical significance testing or confidence intervals, limited runs, and unclear what 'training time' includes in Figure 4

Inconsistent generalization performance: Table 6 (TSPLib) shows mixed results—sometimes worse than baselines (kroB100, kroD100)—with no analysis of failure modes or problem characteristics driving performance

Under-specified technical details: credit assignment function uses ad-hoc piecewise thresholds without justification; utility function weights not ablated; recency bonus Br(t, τi) not formally defined in main text; population size (4) very small—impact on diversity unexplored
Limited baseline comparisons: no comparison with simpler knowledge reuse approaches or ablations on credit assignment schemes; missing traditional EC knowledge management methods
Narrow experimental scope: only synthetic optimization benchmarks; no evaluation on real-world problems; questions about practical cost of multiple LLM calls per generation not addressed
